translationRepairs: The Book of Changes, Kun, first six lines, says: “Treading frost, hard ice arrives.”
The Book of Changes, Kun, first yin line, says: “Treading frost, hard ice arrives.”
Independent review confirms the correction against the chapter text. 初六 is the first yin line of hexagram Kun, not “first six lines.”
The Family, first nine lines, says: “Regulating the household, regret vanishes.”
The Family, first yang line, says: “Regulating the household, regret vanishes.”
Independent review confirms the correction against the chapter text. 初九 is the first yang line of hexagram Jiaren, not “first nine lines.”
Taizu said: “Father Zhu the Classicist studied all his life yet never won a degree; he has a son who commands a circuit—he need not blush before the ancestors.”
Taizu said: “Zhu of the Five Classics studied all his life yet never won a degree; he has a son who commands a circuit—he need not blush before the ancestors.”
Independent review confirms the correction against the chapter text. 朱五經 is an epithet “Zhu of the Five Classics,” not “Father Zhu the Classicist.”
Taizu said: “Zhu the Fifth Classicist read books all his life and never passed the examinations; he has a son who is a military commissioner—no shame before our ancestors.”
Taizu said: “Zhu of the Five Classics read books all his life and never passed the examinations; he has a son who is a military commissioner—no shame before our ancestors.”
Independent review confirms the correction against the chapter text. 五經 names the Five Classics, not an ordinal “Fifth.”
In the autumn of Dazhun 2 the empress fell ill; augurs said she must go home.”
In the autumn of Dashun 2, the empress fell ill; diviners said, “She should return to her native place.”

大順 is Dashun, not Dazhun, and the old field has an unmatched closing quotation mark. Because the Chinese directly quotes the diviners, the revised English restores a complete quoted sentence rather than dropping the quotation.
In autumn of the second year of Dazhun, the empress fell ill; the diviner said: “She should return to her native place.”
In autumn of the second year of Dashun, the empress fell ill; the diviner said: “She should return to her native place.”
Independent review confirms the correction against the chapter text. 大順 is the Tang Dashun reign, conventionally Dashun, not Dazhun.
In Jin Tianfu 3 an edict allowed families to reclaim criminal heads held at the altar; the Last Emperor’s head was released, and Right Palace Gate General An Chongruan buried it with the consort.
In Jin Tianfu 3 an edict allowed families to reclaim criminal heads held at the altar; the Last Emperor’s head was released, and General of the Right Guard An Chongruan buried it with the consort.
Independent review confirms the correction against the chapter text. 右衛將軍 is General of the Right Guard, not “Right Palace Gate General.”
Eight sons by blood: Youyu, then Yougui, Youzhang, Youzhen, Youyong, Youhui, and Youzi, plus the adopted Youwen.
Eight sons: the eldest Youyu, then Yougui, Youzhang, Youzhen, Youyong, Youhui, and Youzi, plus the adopted Youwen.
Independent review confirms the correction against the chapter text. 八子 lists seven blood sons plus one adopted son; “eight sons by blood” invents an eighth biological son.

The stray extra question mark must be removed, but the proposal still closes Quanyu's speech too early. The Chinese quotation continues through s0101, so this opening unit must end without a closing quotation mark.
Cun’s sons were Youning and Youlun.

Cui Yin sent envoys to halt him, but Taizu was convinced that Yin and his circle had murdered Youlun. He demanded their deaths; Zhaozong refused. Taizu then sent Youliang to the capital with troops, invested Kaihua Ward, and killed Yin, Zheng Yuangui of Henan, Wang Jianxun of the Imperial City, Chen Ban of the Flying Dragon Office, Wang Jianxi of the Gate Office, Wang Jianyi of the Reception Office, and the former Left Vice Director Zhang Jun.

Taizu then sent Youliang to the capital with troops, invested Kaihua Ward, and killed Yin, Zheng Yuangui, Metropolitan Prefect of Jingzhao, Wang Jianxun of the Imperial City, Chen Ban of the Flying Dragon Office, Wang Jianxi of the Gate Office, Wang Jianyi of the Reception Office, and the former Left Vice Director Zhang Jun.
Independent review confirms the correction against the chapter text. 京兆尹 is the metropolitan prefect of Jingzhao, not “of Henan.”
He served as acting prefect of Xuzhou.
He served as acting prefect of Xu.
Independent review confirms the correction against the chapter text. 許州 is Xu Prefecture (Xuchang), not 徐州 Xuzhou; the idiomatic field conflates the two.

In the third year of Tianfu of Jin an edict said that heads of criminals long kept in the Grand Temple might be reclaimed by kin for burial; the Last Emperor’s head was then taken out, and Right Palace Gate General An Chongruan was sent to bury it together with the consort.

In the third year of Tianfu of Jin, an edict allowed relatives to reclaim for burial the heads of criminals previously kept at the Grand Altar; the Last Emperor’s head was then brought out, and An Chongruan, General of the Right Guard, was sent to bury it together with the consort.
右衛將軍 is General of the Right Guard, not Right Palace Gate General; the paired literal field is corrected with the reviewed idiomatic field.
The translated editorial note retained a stray Chinese closing bracket; it is normalized as a complete English parenthetical.

Chief Minister Cui Yin sent men to stop Taizu; Taizu believed Youlun had been killed by Yin and the rest, memorialized asking that Yin be executed, and Zhaozong did not consent; Taizu then sent Youliang to the capital; with troops he surrounded Kaihua Ward and killed Yin, Henan prefect Zheng Yuangui, Imperial City Commissioner Wang Jianxun, Flying Dragon Commissioner Chen Ban, Gate Commissioner Wang Jianxi, Reception Commissioner Wang Jianyi, and former Left Vice Director Zhang Jun.

Taizu then sent Youliang to the capital; with troops he surrounded Kaihua Ward and killed Yin, Zheng Yuangui, Metropolitan Prefect of Jingzhao, Imperial City Commissioner Wang Jianxun, Flying Dragon Commissioner Chen Ban, Gate Commissioner Wang Jianxi, Reception Commissioner Wang Jianyi, and former Left Vice Director Zhang Jun.
京兆尹 is Metropolitan Prefect of Jingzhao, not a Henan prefect; the paired literal field is corrected and the long sentence is clarified.
He acted as prefect of Xuzhou.
He held acting charge of Xu Prefecture.
許州 is Xu Prefecture, not Xuzhou; the paired literal field must match the reviewed place correction.
Xuzhou lay near Cai and had suffered great bandit raids; the people were broken; Youyu gathered the scattered and increased households by more than thirty thousand.

Xu Prefecture lay near Cai and had suffered severe bandit raids; its residents were scattered and ruined. Youyu summoned back the displaced and increased the registered households by more than thirty thousand.
許州 is Xu Prefecture, not Xuzhou; the administrative recovery is rendered clearly without changing the reported household increase.
Xuzhou bordered Cai and had been ravaged by raiders; the population was shattered. Youyu brought back refugees and added more than thirty thousand households.
Xu Prefecture bordered Cai and had been ravaged by raiders. Youyu brought back the scattered population and added more than thirty thousand households.
許州 is Xu Prefecture, not Xuzhou; the same place correction must continue through the following sentence.
He was promoted to commander of all armies; with that force he pacified Yan and Yun, then returned to hold Xuzhou.
He was promoted to commander of all armies, took part in pacifying Yan and Yun, and then returned to govern Xu Prefecture.
還領許州 says he returned to govern Xu Prefecture; Xuzhou is the wrong prefecture and the coordination is clarified.
Promoted to commander of all armies, he helped subdue Yan and Yun and then resumed command at Xuzhou.
Promoted to commander of all armies, he helped subdue Yan and Yun and then returned to govern Xu Prefecture.
還領許州 says he returned to govern Xu Prefecture, not Xuzhou.
